505d7a5a8b248d70.label: MAKE
505d7a5a8b248d70.summary: Neuroscientists discover crows make complex visual discrimination decisions twice as fast as humans and primates. Hook: 'While humans deliberate, crows make split-second visual choices twice as fast as primates—using a brain the size of a walnut.'
505d7a5a8b248d70.notes:
- Published by neurobiologists testing avian decision reaction times
- Corvid nidopallium processes visual stimuli significantly faster than mammalian neocortex
- Demonstrates convergent evolution of intelligence across completely different brain architectures

6c2d97c1b21a8eb2.notes:
- Analyzed ages and orbits of hundreds of thousands of stars
